Messages.Author: gabusanvtes
Messages.Body:
during a combat, a vampire play majesty at superior (to end combat and
untap) and the other walk of flame+Rotschreck. The majesty vampire is
sent to torpor. The question: is he tapped or not?

Thanks a lot

Messages.Author: Colin McGuigan
Messages.Body:
gabusanvtes wrote:



Tapped. Rotschreck takes effect before strikes resolve, so the Majesty
does not take effect.

--Colin McGuigan

I would say, that this is a tricky one.

Majesty ends combat and untaps the vampire "before combat ends", it is
not a regular strike, it is a s:ce. Rotschreck is also a CE effect.
so in my oppinion i would say, that the vampire untaps from majesty
(like if both combatants play a majesty, they both untap, because CE
strikes resolve at the same time), BUT ends up tapped because of
Rotschreck card text "...this vampire is tapped..."

just my opinion

Messages.Author: Colin McGuigan
Messages.Body:
Jyhad_addict wrote:
> I would say, that this is a tricky one.

You can argue with LSJ all you want. =P

> Majesty ends combat and untaps the vampire "before combat ends", it is
> not a regular strike, it is a s:ce.

But it is still a strike. Notice the "S" in "S:CE".

> Rotschreck is also a CE effect.

But not a strike. This is key.

> so in my oppinion i would say, that the vampire untaps from majesty
> (like if both combatants play a majesty, they both untap, because CE
> strikes resolve at the same time), BUT ends up tapped because of
> Rotschreck card text "...this vampire is tapped..."

Striking is divided up into three phases: strike declaration, strike
resolution, and then damage handling. Rotschreck takes place during
strike declaration. Before strike resolution. Therefore, none of the
strikes go off -- if the opponent used, eg, a Flash Grenade, the other
minion (if a vampire) would not tap, an Oubliette would not do the point
of damage, etc.

> P.S. what happens if i am the acting minion and i end combat (e.g. via
> sup alpha glint), can the opposing minion play any before range stuff
> like illusions of the kindred ? i think not, but i'd like an official
> answer.

Correct. Once you play superior Alpha Glint, combat is over (barring
Psyche! or Telepathic Tracking, as usual).

--Colin McGuigan
